items.headline: VOLTA infostealer uses Claude, Gemini and Kimi to profile stolen data
items.summary: Security researchers identified a new Windows infostealer, VOLTA, that feeds stolen credentials, sessions and crypto-wallet data into commercial AI models to automatically rank and prioritize victims. It's a concrete example of attackers weaponizing mainstream chatbots to scale cybercrime operations.

items.headline: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro usage limits after subscriber backlash
items.summary: OpenAI reversed a planned 50% cut to Pro-tier limits and instead doubled usage caps for its Pro and Business Premium plans without raising prices, following user backlash over the proposed reduction. ChatGPT Plus limits remain unchanged.

items.headline: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
items.summary: TechCrunch reports growing investor unease over AI infrastructure spending, noting that Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft plan to spend more than $740 billion on capex this year while Alphabet posted $9.1 billion in negative free cash flow last quarter — a sign the AI buildout's economics are drawing sharper scrutiny.

items.headline: Anthropic files IPO prospectus targeting a $2 trillion valuation
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing discloses a roughly $42 billion net loss for 2025, a decade-long compute spending commitment of at least $518 billion, and explicit warnings that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" — with close to a third of the prospectus devoted to risk factors.

items.headline: Mistral releases open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model
items.summary: Mistral AI published downloadable weights for its flagship Large 4 model on Hugging Face under a modified-MIT open license, days after debuting it in preview — a notable open-weight counterpoint to closed frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic.

items.headline: Tesla begins high-volume Optimus production as reservations loom
items.summary: Tesla reportedly started building its Optimus humanoid robot on a high-volume production line in Fremont, California, with an industry expert suggesting customer reservations could open as early as December, though Elon Musk disputed that timing on X.

items.headline: Figure's humanoid robots work paid shifts at BMW as Boston Dynamics' Atlas eyes Hyundai factories
items.summary: Figure AI's Figure 03 robot is reportedly doing logistics-sequencing work at BMW's Spartanburg plant while Figure's BotQ factory ramps toward roughly one robot built per hour, and Boston Dynamics' electric Atlas is moving toward industrial deployment, with Hyundai reportedly planning tens of thousands of units for its factories.

items.headline: Waymo expands robotaxi service across five more U.S. cities
items.summary: Waymo added nearly 250 square miles of coverage spanning Los Angeles, Nashville, Orlando, San Diego and the San Francisco Bay Area, part of a push toward 1 million weekly paid trips by year's end and a previously announced plan to launch in Toronto in 2028.
